title: Design layer roll-up — the whole vertical slice for one project (GET /api/projects/<id>/design-layer)
description: The read the Workbench evidence panel and the standalone-chain acceptance both hang on, and the one row in this family that assembles rather than serves: `src/design_lab/design_layer.py` get_design_layer re-reads the brief page, the direction page, every binding row and the packaged design-system catalog, then decides two nullable answers on its own. Those two are the reason this needed a contract instead of a comment. P0-02: `chosen_direction` is null unless a direction really carries `chosen=1` — it must never fall back to the most recently created direction, which would fabricate a Human Choice that never happened. P0-D: `active_binding` is null unless the binding belongs to THAT chosen direction — switching the choice from A to B leaves B unbound, so the field must go null rather than keep pointing at A. Both are expressed as `oneOf [null, record]` so a silent fallback to the wrong row is a schema violation, not a plausible-looking panel. `briefs` and `directions` are the FIRST PAGE only: the roll-up calls the paging readers with no cursor, and the 100-item cap the writer applies is bound here so a reader cannot take a truncated slice for the project's whole history. Record shapes are `$ref`'d from their owners (`brief-readback.schema.json`, `design-record-v1.schema.json`), never restated; `design_system` is owned here because the catalog projection is what this document creates — four keys measured out of `catalog()` over the four packaged manifests on 2026-10-23, with `evidence_level` bounded to the E0-E5 ladder AGENTS.md defines and the name bounded by `DESIGN_SYSTEM_NAME_PATTERN`.
